accounting.rationale: Defines the attribute's domain as limitations on module entities; it is not PRIVATE accessibility or a separate executable obligation.
The operative restrictions and exceptions are C856-C860 and p2-p3, not a new no-op classifier.
Declaration, accessibility and association retain their defining scopes in 14.2, 8.5.2 and 19.5.1.
Exception to the association-change prohibition. The resulting undefined status is governed by 19.5.2.5, not a processor choice to preserve association and not an inquiry-safe value.
Only deallocation other than through the protected pointer is the stated outside-owner exception. C860 still excludes direct use-associated pointer deallocation.
BLOCK completion can make the target undefined; no post-lifetime target read or ASSOCIATED inquiry is authorized.
RETURN-induced target undefinition is an explicit exception; target-lifetime and argument-association rules still apply.
END-induced target undefinition is retained separately from normal defined disassociation or an extended target lifetime.
Normative attribute propagation to every subobject supplies the premises of C859/C860 and p2. It is not an independent storage-copy effect or a reason for a no-op S requirement.
The parent object must actually have PROTECTED; accessibility alone does not supply it.

Retain elements, sections, substrings and components under their own designator rules. Under 9.4.2p5 a pointer component is a subobject in association-status contexts, but its target is not a subobject of the containing object.
Each subobject inherits PROTECTED, with the nonpointer/pointer restrictions selected for that actual subject. Do not invent an explicit PROTECTED component declaration.
The complete temperature module example continues on PDF132. It illustrates an owner-module setter, not exclusive permission for one procedure name or a normative floating-point invariant.
The shown setter accesses the module variables within their owner; a caller passing a protected variable to an OUT/INOUT dummy is a different context.
Consistency of the two illustrative temperatures is not an additional S requirement, rounding oracle, privacy rule or atomicity guarantee.

requirements.title: PROTECTED is specified only in a module specification part
requirements.definition: The PROTECTED attribute may be specified only in the specification part of a module. A main program, submodule, procedure, BLOCK or interface body's own specification part is not the module specification part, even when textually nested in a module.

pending.module-specification-forms: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete provider modules with one locally declared INTEGER variable, once with a PROTECTED attr-spec and once with a separate PROTECTED statement. No COMMON, PARAMETER, imported entity or duplicate attribute; optional client USE/read preserves PUBLIC accessibility.
pending.interface-body-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: a complete provider has an ordinary explicit interface body with a typed scalar dummy carrying PROTECTED. Remove PROTECTED and retain the complete matching procedure definition; the interface body's scope is distinct even inside a module specification part.
pending.submodule-scope-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: ancestor module declares a separate module procedure and a conforming descendant implements it; a separate ordinary INTEGER declared directly in the submodule has PROTECTED. Delete that attribute only. Host access to an ancestor's protected entity is a different, permitted owner/descendant premise.

requirements.oracle:
For isolated numbered violations require detection/reporting under 4.2p2(3), with an accepted complete minimal repair and cause tied to the PROTECTED declaration's scope. Valid controls are compile admission, not runtime protection evidence. R858 and type-declaration syntax keep their own owners.

C856 module-specification diagnostic fixtures: three compile/diagnose negatives put the PROTECTED attribute on an otherwise ordinary INTEGER entity in a main program specification part, an external subroutine specification part, and a BLOCK specification part. Each paired control deletes only the PROTECTED attr-spec and runs the complete source. The diagnostic is anchored on the declaration line and must report PROTECTED placement rather than an unsupported facility, crash, missing provider, or unrelated syntax error.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Module placement is necessary, not sufficient: C857/C858 and USE-associated attribute restrictions still apply. Neither a PRIVATE substitution nor a missing provider/interface is a conforming repair. No mandatory fatal rejection, rule-code spelling or compiler-specific wording follows.

C856 module-specification diagnostic boundaries: only main-program, external-subroutine and BLOCK local declarations are covered. Module specification forms that use a separate PROTECTED statement, interface-body scope, submodule scope, contained-procedure locals and respecification of imported entities remain pending. Reporting is required, but fatal rejection, exact text and rule-number spelling are not.

requirements.title: PROTECTED applies to a variable or procedure pointer
requirements.definition: An entity with PROTECTED must be a variable or a procedure pointer. A data pointer is a variable; an ordinary procedure and a named constant are not admitted by this rule.

pending.ordinary-procedure-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: a complete module declares an ordinary external procedure by PROCEDURE with a complete abstract interface and PROTECTED but no POINTER; supply its matching external definition as a separate complete unit. Delete only PROTECTED for the ordinary-procedure repair. The separate procedure-pointer admission facet does not need an unassociated invocation.

requirements.oracle:
Compile admission for the two allowed entity categories and a numbered reporting/control contrast for excluded categories. Resolve names and procedure interfaces before attributing a C857 report. Procedure declaration rules and PARAMETER classification remain canonical dependencies.

C857 admitted/excluded entity fixtures: one run/positive-control module declares an INTEGER nonpointer variable, a data pointer variable initially NULL, and a procedure pointer, all with PROTECTED in the module specification part. Owner procedures associate the pointers and the client observes the defined scalar value, the data-pointer association, and a procedure-pointer call result. A separate numbered negative gives PROTECTED to an INTEGER PARAMETER named constant; deleting only PARAMETER yields the paired variable control.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
An attribute does not convert a named constant into a variable or a plain procedure into a pointer. Generic wrong-context, unknown-name, interface, unsupported-facility, crash or resource diagnostics cannot corroborate the category restriction.

C857 admitted/excluded entity boundaries: the positive entity fixture covers default INTEGER variables, data pointers, and one non-elemental INTEGER function procedure pointer. It does not dereference a disassociated pointer. Only PARAMETER/named-constant exclusion is diagnosed here; ordinary-procedure exclusion remains pending.

requirements.title: A protected entity is not in a common block
requirements.definition: An entity with PROTECTED must not be in a common block. Both named and blank common are within this exclusion.

pending.named-common-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: a module declares one ordinary INTEGER x, COMMON /shared/ x, and PROTECTED x. No initializer or BIND attribute. Delete PROTECTED only, keeping the otherwise valid named COMMON declaration; require the protected/common incompatibility cause.
pending.blank-common-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: the same bounded module uses COMMON x with no block name. Remove only PROTECTED. No DATA or declaration initializer is allowed on this common member; unrelated COMMON diagnostics are not C858 evidence.

requirements.oracle:
Standard-required reporting of this numbered incompatibility with an accepted one-predicate repair. The forbidden subject is the protected common member, not merely the presence of COMMON or its storage syntax.

C858 ordinary module control fixture: one run/positive-control module keeps a protected INTEGER out of COMMON, sets it through an owner procedure, and lets the client read the value. This covers only the ordinary module-side control for the common-block exclusion.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Do not initialize a common member outside a conforming block-data context, import it by USE into another COMMON declaration, or substitute a forbidden procedure pointer/allocatable/coarray member. Such failures have different owners.

C858 ordinary module control boundaries: only the ordinary protected-module-variable control is selected. Named and blank COMMON diagnostics remain pending because they need their own one-property controls and current frozen LFortran accepts the invalid COMMON forms rather than diagnosing C858.

requirements.title: A use-associated protected nonpointer is not defined or used as a pointer target
requirements.source: 8.5.15 C859, including all three prohibited context alternatives; J3/24-007, physical PDF131.
requirements.definition: A nonpointer object with PROTECTED that is accessed by use association must not appear in a variable definition context, as a data-target, or as an initial-data-target. The fifteen variable-definition-context items remain defined by 19.6.7; all type, scope, argument and construct premises must hold before this constraint is isolated.

pending.io-implied-do-variable: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(2): use the imported protected INTEGER as the existing implied-DO variable in a formatted WRITE to an unprotected local character buffer. Do not introduce a new integer-type-spec index that shadows it. Remove PROTECTED only.
pending.read-input-item: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(3): READ from a defined local character input variable containing '17' into the imported protected INTEGER. A character literal is not substituted for the internal-file variable. Remove PROTECTED only.
pending.namelist-read: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(4): declare the client NAMELIST with the USE-associated protected INTEGER as a member and read it from a defined local buffer containing the matching group/member input. Remove PROTECTED only. A namelist used only for output is a separate readonly control.
pending.internal-file-write: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(5): the imported protected fixed-length CHARACTER is the internal-file variable of a conforming formatted WRITE of an ordinary INTEGER. Remove PROTECTED only; keep unit, format and data-item typing unchanged.
pending.size-specifier: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(6): after a valid scratch formatted connection and record setup, a nonadvancing READ uses the protected INTEGER in SIZE=, with ADVANCE='NO' and local IOSTAT handling. The input item is unprotected. Remove PROTECTED only; unrelated I/O restrictions are not corroboration.
pending.iomsg-specifier: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(6): use an imported protected CHARACTER variable as IOMSG= on an otherwise valid I/O statement with local IOSTAT. Remove PROTECTED only. No error-free IOMSG value or mandatory message wording is asserted.
pending.inquire-output: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(7): protected LOGICAL appears in EXIST= of INQUIRE(FILE=local_name,...). Remove PROTECTED only. FILE=, ID= and UNIT= are the stated input exceptions; a readonly FILE= control is bounded now, while a valid pending-request premise is required before any ID= runtime example.
pending.newunit-specifier: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(8): OPEN(NEWUNIT=protected_integer,STATUS='SCRATCH',IOSTAT=local_status) uses valid remaining specifiers. Remove PROTECTED only and close a successfully opened unit in the control; do not require a particular assigned unit number.
pending.allocate-deallocate-object: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(9): protected module allocatable INTEGER array is used as an allocate-object. For DEALLOCATE, an owner-module preparation procedure first allocates it. Remove PROTECTED only. Do not allocate a procedure pointer or deallocate an unallocated object in the control.
pending.stat-errmsg-specifiers: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(9): separate bounded ALLOCATE/DEALLOCATE variants place a protected INTEGER in STAT= or protected CHARACTER in ERRMSG=, using an unprotected eligible allocation object and local STAT when needed. Delete the selected PROTECTED attribute only; no unspecified error text or value is an oracle.
pending.notify-variable-context: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(9): module exports a protected scalar NOTIFY_TYPE coarray and an unprotected INTEGER coarray. Separate variants isolate client payload[THIS_IMAGE(),NOTIFY=notice]=17 or client NOTIFY WAIT(notice); the matching drain or prior notification occurs through a no-notice-argument owner API using host access. Remove PROTECTED only. Keep the notify-variable noncoindexed and satisfy C1177/C1178/C1611-C1614; no second forbidden client use, private count read or unsupported-feature failure earns credit.
pending.construct-selector-definition: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(11): bounded ASSOCIATE(alias=>protected_integer) followed by alias=17. Remove PROTECTED only; replacing the selector with a value expression is not a valid writable control. SELECT TYPE/CHANGE TEAM extensions need their complete eligibility proof; SELECT RANK is explicitly gated by C839/C1155 and cannot use a directly imported fixed-rank module variable.
pending.event-post-wait: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(12): separate variants isolate a client EVENT POST on this image or local EVENT WAIT using the protected scalar EVENT_TYPE coarray. The matching owner-side drain or preparation post uses host access and no protected actual argument. Remove PROTECTED only; keep C1183/C1184/C1603-C1606 and never inspect private event representation or wait without a prior post.
pending.lock-unlock: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(13): separate client LOCK and client UNLOCK variants use a protected scalar LOCK_TYPE coarray. Owner APIs using host access provide the matching release or prior acquisition on the same executing image, without passing the protected lock as a defining actual. Remove PROTECTED only; preserve C1189/C1607-C1610 and avoid a second forbidden client use, double locking or an unheld unlock.
pending.acquired-lock-result: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(14): unprotected valid lock coarray with protected LOGICAL in ACQUIRED_LOCK=. Remove PROTECTED on that result variable only; unlock only after successful acquisition in the complete control. The lock object itself is not the forbidden subject.
pending.form-team-result: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, item(15): protected scalar TEAM_TYPE is the result variable of FORM TEAM(1,team), executed by all active images if the control is later run. Remove PROTECTED only. Positive team number, no conflicting NEW_INDEX, valid intrinsic type identity and no private component access are required.
pending.initial-data-target: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: client initializes a compatible data pointer to the imported protected module TARGET. Module scope supplies SAVE; all selectors are constant and nonvector. Delete PROTECTED only. Preserve C770/C812 target eligibility rather than repairing by removing TARGET or inventing an unsaved target.
pending.subobjects-and-renaming: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: bounded renamed imported scalar and ordinary array element/section, CHARACTER substring and public ordinary derived component variants inherit PROTECTED under p3. Remove the parent's single PROTECTED specification. Pointer-component association contexts instead remain C860; pointee targets are not such subobjects.
pending.always-defined-empty-contexts: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: protected INTEGER array of constant extent zero is assigned a scalar, and protected CHARACTER(0) is assigned ''. Remove PROTECTED only. 19.6.2's always-defined empty values do not waive a syntactic variable-definition-context prohibition, allocation eligibility or presence.

requirements.oracle:
Every negative keeps the three subject premises: nonpointer, PROTECTED and use-associated. A complete provider/client and a source-minimal accepted repair must isolate the named prohibited context. Standard-required numbered reporting is not mandatory fatal rejection, printed C859, or a prescribed message. The external context enumeration is retained at 19.6.7, not fabricated as new original C859 list items.

C859 use-associated nonpointer context fixtures: four compile/diagnose negatives use a complete provider/client pair where the subject is a nonpointer object with PROTECTED accessed by USE association. The selected forbidden contexts are intrinsic assignment, ordinary DO variable, actual argument corresponding to an explicit-interface INTENT(OUT) nonpointer dummy, and data-target in pointer assignment. Each repair deletes only PROTECTED at the provider and runs. A separate readonly control USEs and renames protected integers, reads them, and passes one to an INTENT(IN) dummy without any definition context.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Keep all fifteen context items, but do not invent an inadmissible construct to instantiate one: C839/C1155 prevent the naive module-variable SELECT RANK example. Event/lock/notify controls must satisfy their own type/coarray/context constraints. Pointer-dummy INTENT(IN) is not a blanket repair for a protected nonpointer TARGET: 15.5.2.8 requires a valid pointer-assignment target. READ/WRITE/inquiry values, failed allocation, unavailable language facilities, crashes and unrelated diagnostics cannot substitute for the isolated compile contrast.

C859 use-associated nonpointer context boundaries: only assignment, ordinary DO, OUT actual, data-target, and readonly USE controls are selected. READ, NAMELIST, internal-file WRITE, SIZE/IOMSG/INQUIRE/NEWUNIT, allocation outputs, coarray synchronization outputs, construct selectors, initial-data-targets, subobjects, empty contexts and the remaining 19.6.7 families remain pending.

requirements.title: A use-associated protected pointer is excluded from association-changing contexts
requirements.definition: A pointer with PROTECTED accessed by use association must not appear in a pointer association context. The four context families are defined in 19.6.8. Data-target definition is not itself pointer association, and allocation forms admit data pointers, not arbitrary procedure pointers.

pending.nullify-procedure-pointer: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: same NULLIFY context for a protected procedure pointer with a complete explicit interface. Remove PROTECTED only; no attempted procedure call is needed.
pending.procedure-pointer-assignment: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: protected imported procedure pointer is assigned a live compatible non-elemental module procedure. Remove PROTECTED only; retain the complete explicit interfaces and correct function/subroutine category.
pending.allocate-deallocate-data-pointer: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, third family: separate client ALLOCATE and DEALLOCATE variants use a protected imported data pointer. For DEALLOCATE, an owner-host API with no protected actual first allocates the whole matching target; owner-side cleanup avoids another forbidden client context in the ALLOCATE variant. Remove PROTECTED only. No procedure-pointer allocation, unallocated or allocatable target, or active dummy/associate alias is a valid control.
pending.data-pointer-out-inout-actual: PENDING compile diagnostic/control, fourth family: protected actual data pointer corresponds to an explicit-interface pointer OUT or INOUT dummy. Remove PROTECTED only, or use a complete read-only pointer INTENT(IN) interface/body control. The actual remains a pointer, not a nonpointer target masquerading as an OUT pointer variable.
pending.procedure-pointer-out-inout-actual: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: procedure-pointer actual corresponds to a matching procedure-pointer OUT/INOUT dummy. Remove PROTECTED only or change to an IN-only read-only interface/body control; preserve characteristics and do not substitute a function result for a required pointer-variable actual.
pending.pointer-subobject: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: public pointer component of an imported protected ordinary record inherits PROTECTED in its association-status context. Apply NULLIFY or compatible => to that component; remove PROTECTED from the containing object only. Do not spell an illegal PROTECTED component attribute or confuse its target with a subobject.

requirements.oracle:
A same-input minimal repair must make the selected association context legal; the negative report must concern changing a use-associated protected pointer. Numbered C860 reporting is separate from fatal rejection, a compiler code policy or a wrong-kind/interface/lifetime error.

C860 protected pointer context fixtures: two compile/diagnose negatives use a USE-associated protected data pointer in pointer association contexts: NULLIFY and data-pointer assignment to a live local TARGET. Each repair deletes only PROTECTED and runs. The positive control queries a protected data pointer with ASSOCIATED and calls a protected procedure pointer after owner-side association, leaving both associations unchanged outside the module.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Direct DEALLOCATE through this pointer is not the p2 other-route exception. A module-owner callee does not waive the protected actual's OUT/INOUT caller context. Unspecified INTENT is not a promise that the actual's association may be changed: p2 and argument-alias rules still apply.

C860 protected pointer context boundaries: only NULLIFY, data-pointer assignment and read-only association query/procedure call controls are covered. Procedure-pointer NULLIFY/assignment, allocation/deallocation, OUT/INOUT pointer dummies and pointer subobjects remain pending.

requirements.title: A protected nonpointer is not definable outside its defining module and descendants
requirements.source: 8.5.15 p2 scope qualification and first bullet; J3/24-007, physical PDF131.
requirements.definition: Other than within the module in which the entity is given PROTECTED or within any descendant of that module, a protected nonpointer object is not definable. Association and aliasing do not turn a nondefinable ultimate object into a definable one. This scope rule is not PRIVATE accessibility.

pending.descendant-host-setter-control: PENDING bounded run/positive-control: ancestor module declares a public separate module setter; a genuine submodule descendant implements it and changes the ancestor entity by host association. A complete client verifies 17 then 19 and visits. Retain C1412/C1577 and exact interfaces; an unrelated module or mere USE re-export is not a descendant.
pending.foreign-host-route-restriction: PENDING source-use/optional-policy gate: a client that USEs x contains a helper accessing the same protected object through its host and attempting definition outside the owner/descendants. The conforming repair removes PROTECTED at the owner, not by shadowing x. Resolve the exact C859/name-association duty before a negative case; no automatic required diagnosis or runtime result follows merely from p2.
pending.alias-to-protected-target-restriction: PENDING source-use/optional-policy gate: owner module exposes a pointer result to a defined protected TARGET with live module storage; an outside client attempts to define that ultimate target through an ordinary alias. Remove PROTECTED from the ultimate target for the conforming repair. Confirm all pointer-result/target and caller restrictions before admission; never treat an unprotected alias as permission to mutate a protected target or execute the violation as a required trap.

requirements.oracle:
Conforming scope controls are positive-control evidence, not a proof of every forbidden definition. For a concrete forbidden form that satisfies C859, retain C859 primary ownership and its required reporting basis; a p2-only proposal needs an independently declared additional diagnostic policy, a valid minimal repair and the exact ultimate-object/cause argument.

S8.5.15-001 owner-module definition control fixture: one run/effect fixture gives a PUBLIC module INTEGER the PROTECTED attribute, mutates it only inside the owner module by a setter, and has a client observe the nonzero values 17 and 29 after separate calls. No protected object is passed by the client as an OUT or INOUT actual.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
The owner is the module where the attribute is given, not any module that imports the entity. Host association retains attributes but does not make a foreign host part of that owner tree. No blanket diagnostic obligation, exclusive-setter rule, copy/address oracle or aliasing waiver is inferred.

S8.5.15-001 owner-module definition boundaries: only direct owner-module mutation by a setter is covered. Descendant submodule mutation, foreign host routes and alias-to-protected-target restrictions remain pending. This is positive conforming evidence, not a manufactured diagnostic for the prose restriction.

requirements.title: A protected pointer's association is preserved outside its owner subject to exact target-lifetime exceptions
requirements.source: 8.5.15 p2 scope qualification, second bullet and its exceptions; J3/24-007, physical PDF131.
requirements.definition: Outside the defining module and its descendants, a protected pointer's association status must not be changed, except that it may become undefined when its target is deallocated other than through it, or becomes undefined on BLOCK completion or RETURN/END. This protects association, not an independently definable unprotected target's value, and does not prolong any target or procedure-host lifetime.

pending.module-descendant-association-control: PENDING bounded run/positive-control: owner module and a genuine descendant set/reset a protected data pointer through host access, without passing the imported pointer as OUT/INOUT at the client. Client ASSOCIATED checks use two live distinct scalar module TARGETs and a known NULL reset, with independent visit guards and no address comparison.
pending.no-intent-pointer-alias-restriction: PENDING source-use/optional-policy gate: an outside helper's pointer dummy has no INTENT, so C860's explicit OUT/INOUT actual context is not assumed; an attempted NULLIFY through that alias changes the protected actual's association and must still satisfy p2. A minimal conforming repair deletes the association-changing statement, retaining a read-only check and visit observer. Complete interfaces, defined association and 15.5.2.14 are prerequisites; no standard-required diagnostic is inferred without a separate numbered/scope basis.
pending.other-route-deallocation-context: PENDING bounded run/positive-control for legality only: owner allocates the whole data-pointer target and defines it; client associates an ordinary alias and legally deallocates through that alias. Do not query or dereference the now-undefined protected pointer. Call an owner-side unconditional NULLIFY reset before a later safe false ASSOCIATED check. Observe calls/completion, not an undefined-status value; direct deallocation through the imported protected pointer remains C860.
pending.block-target-end-context: PENDING bounded run/positive-control for legality only: a client BLOCK's ordinary unsaved scalar TARGET is associated with the protected pointer by an owner setter whose scalar TARGET dummy satisfies 15.5.2.5p9. After END BLOCK, do not inquire about the protected pointer or former target until an owner-side reset. Entry/exit/reset markers are independent; this does not directly observe undefined association.
pending.return-end-target-context: PENDING bounded run/positive-control for legality only: an external caller-owned subprogram supplies a defined unsaved scalar TARGET to the same owner setter while live, then terminates through RETURN or END. Main performs no dangling inquiry and invokes an unconditional owner reset first. Observe visits and ordinary copied snapshots while defined, not persistence of a dead target.

requirements.oracle:
Numbered C860 contexts retain C860 ownership. These conforming controls exercise owner access, legal target-value operations or allowed lifetime-ending contexts, without claiming direct observation of undefined status. Every future runtime control needs complete calls, defined values, live association before inquiries, independent literals/visits/completion and supported-mode qualification; compiler consensus is not its source oracle.

S8.5.15-002 protected pointer target/call controls: one run/effect fixture associates a protected data pointer with an unprotected live module TARGET inside the owner, then the client defines that target through the pointer and verifies the independent target value and unchanged association. A separate run/effect fixture associates a protected procedure pointer inside the owner and the client calls it while leaving association unchanged.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Undefined association is not defined disassociation and cannot be queried with ASSOCIATED. Target deallocation must satisfy 9.7.3.3, not deallocate an ordinary static or allocatable target through a pointer. The protected pointer cannot be reset by an outside NULLIFY merely to make an inquiry safe. Any proposed outside-owner internal-procedure-host-death example needs its own p2/19.5.2.5(8) source argument and remains outside this packet's finite contexts.

S8.5.15-002 protected pointer target/call boundaries: only a scalar INTEGER data pointer target definition and a live module procedure-pointer call are covered. Other-route deallocation, BLOCK/RETURN/END target-lifetime exceptions, descendant association controls and no-INTENT pointer-alias restrictions remain pending. Frozen LFortran rejects the conforming target-definition fixture by treating assignment through the pointer as assignment to the protected pointer object; the case is retained because the reference compiler runs it and p2 protects association, not target value.

review_rationale: Source registration renewed after binding Clause 8 PROTECTED attribute fixtures (batch174). Classification and pending plans re-verified by an independent reviewer against 8.5.15, 19.6.7 and 19.6.8; the remaining C859 and C860 contexts stay pending with bounded plans.
